input.question: How do CPUs decode and run instructions ? Do they have a dedicated circuit for each instruction / opcode of their set ?
input.ground_truth: > Do they have a dedicated circuit for each instruction / opcode of their set ? Basically, yes. The CPU has multiple circuits dedicated to each specific instruction or set of related instructions. Each of these circuits basically outputs a bit which denotes whether the appropriate component is active, and maybe other bits determining what type of operation it should perform, and where it should take its input from.

Now, the robot has a special book (called the "instruction set") that tells it what each secret code means. When the robot gets a secret code, it looks it up in its book.

But the robot doesn’t have a special button for every single code. Instead, it has a smart helper inside (called a "decoder"). The decoder looks at the secret code and figures out what job to do. Then, it tells different parts of the robot (like its arms or wheels) how to do that job.

Some robots have a special spot for the most common jobs, so they can do them really fast. But for other jobs, the decoder helps the robot figure out what to do by following the steps in its book.

So, the CPU doesn’t have a separate button for every job, but it has a smart way to understand and do each job using its decoder and some special parts.
